documents.title: Privacy policy
documents.summary: Local-first by default, minimum collection by purpose, and explicit consent before optional diagnostics or measurement.

sections.heading: What this public site stores
sections.body: This phase uses only strictly necessary locale and navigation state. It does not use optional analytics, advertising, cross-site tracking, or a cookie banner.

sections.heading: Collection points
sections.body: The public support and compatibility pages do not submit personal or diagnostic data. A future collection point must state its purpose, required fields, retention, sharing, and revocation before consent.

sections.heading: Retention and sharing
sections.body: No support case, account, device, billing, or diagnostic record is created by the Phase 3 public experience. Therefore none of those records is retained or shared.

sections.heading: Your choices
sections.body: Optional measurement will remain off until granular consent exists. Future consent must be reversible without removing access to safety, recovery, or public documentation.

sections.heading: Accountability
sections.body: Questions, correction requests, and future data-rights requests use the accountable privacy contact above. Phase 4 must add authenticated request authority before any request is presented as submitted.

history.summary: Initial public policy for the deterministic, no-collection Phase 3 experience.

documents.title: Terms of use
documents.summary: The current website is an information and deterministic preview surface, not a checkout or optimization authority.

sections.heading: Current service boundary
sections.body: Phase 3 public pages provide product, compatibility, evidence, documentation, release, and support information. They do not sell a plan, bind a device, modify Windows, or create an entitlement.

sections.heading: Commercial terms
sections.body: No price, billing period, renewal, tax, cancellation, refund, device rule, or expiration effect is active because checkout authority is unavailable. Any future offer must publish all of those terms before confirmation.

sections.heading: Compatibility and evidence
sections.body: Compatibility depends on the Windows lifecycle, architecture, hardware, game, drivers, and the available validation evidence. Public material never guarantees a gain on an unobserved machine.

sections.heading: Safe use
sections.body: Do not treat preview content as permission to run scripts or make unsupported system changes. Use canonical documentation and recovery paths; never bypass an integrity or availability block.

sections.heading: Changes
sections.body: Material changes receive a new version, effective date, plain-language summary, and retained history. A stale term cannot silently remain actionable.

history.summary: Initial no-checkout, no-native-authority terms for Phase 3.

documents.title: Security and trust
documents.summary: Least privilege, signed artifacts, explicit authority boundaries, runtime validation, and recoverable operations define the product boundary.

sections.heading: Authority boundaries
sections.body: The public website has no account, administrative, payment, device, or native optimization authority. Public, account, and admin applications remain separate origins and shells.

sections.heading: Desktop safety direction
sections.body: The renderer remains unprivileged. Future privileged operations must be operation-specific, authenticated, allowlisted, audited, and paired with exact recovery; arbitrary remote scripts are prohibited.

sections.heading: Artifact trust
sections.body: A public download remains blocked until publisher, signature, SHA-256, artifact, manifest, compatibility, and release policy agree. There is no continue-anyway path.

sections.heading: Reporting
sections.body: Potential vulnerabilities should use the responsible disclosure process. Public status reports explain user impact without exposing sensitive internal details.

history.summary: Initial public statement of Phase 3 security boundaries and future native-operation requirements.

disclosure.title: Responsible disclosure
disclosure.summary: Report a potential vulnerability through a scoped, safe channel.
scope: Liiiraa-owned public web origins and published Liiiraa Boost artifacts
Reproducible security behavior that can be described without personal data
Integrity, authorization, privacy, or recovery failures
prohibitedContent: Passwords, access tokens, payment data, or unrelated personal information
Destructive testing, denial of service, persistence, or access beyond the minimum proof
Public disclosure before a safe response window has been coordinated
disclosure.response: We will acknowledge a usable report, validate its scope, and provide a status update through the reporting channel. Timing depends on severity and reproducibility; no bounty or payment is promised.

history.summary: Initial reporting scope and safe-channel policy.

status.title: Operational status
status.summary: Public information is available. Download, account authority, and native optimization are product-availability boundaries, not service incidents.

components.name: Public trusted download
components.detail: No publicly trusted installer has been approved; this is a declared release gate.

components.name: Account and remote authority
components.detail: The account preview lets visitors inspect the experience without changing remote data or actions.

status.incidentHistoryEmpty: No confirmed public service incident has been published. Future entries will name the affected component, user impact, timestamped updates, and resolution without exposing sensitive internals.
